thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 — runtime pods in us-west-2a reporting repeated CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Autoscaler triggered. Incident ID inc-2026-04-12-836

morgan: seeing ~120 5xxs/min on /v1/chat and lots of pod restarts (runtime-main). Node gcpu-034 flapping.

isha: I'm on it. Quick question — is this mostly low-latency traffic (short seq) or long-context jobs?

morgan: mostly long-context loopback tests and some customer production traffic with long prompt prefixes. KV cache fills up then paging goes noisy.

sanjay: logs show paged-attn allocator failing to compact: "alloc_page: no contiguous pages available" and gradual KV fragmentation metrics rising over last 3 hours. snippet:
```
2026-04-12T03:21:10Z runtime[pid=4589]: kvcache: resident_pages=123456 free_pages=312 alloc_failures=42
2026-04-12T03:22:45Z runtime[pid=4589]: pager: fragmentation=0.78 compactions=3 slow_evictions=89
2026-04-12T03:25:01Z runtime[pid=4589]: cuda-oom @ attention_paged.cu: allocate() failed: out of memory
```

alex: immediate mitigations we can do quickly: 1) reduce concurrent batch_size to 1 for affected routes, 2) enable kv_pager.force_compact, 3) cordon+drain the flapping node and restart runtime pods on a fresh node.

lena: customer-impact: 5 orgs reported timeouts, one enterprise customer (acme-inc) saw 504s for chat. CS alerted them and asked for ETA. They want an update in 30m.

ops-bot: Pager created: SRE oncall + eng-runtime. Escalation level: SEV2. Link: https://internal.pager/redwood/incidents/inc-2026-04-12-836

isha: I'll apply config changes to the runtime config map and roll the deployment with a small batch size. Morgan, can you cordon gcpu-034? I'll trigger kv compaction flag after config rollout.

morgan: cordoning gcpu-034 now:
```
kubectl cordon gcpu-034
kubectl drain gcpu-034 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

sanjay: also set env REDWOOD_KV_DEBUG=1 on new pods to collect kv allocation traces (will increase logs). run:
```
kubectl set env deploy/runtime REDWOOD_KV_DEBUG=1
kubectl patch cm runtime-config -p '{"data":{"kv_pager.force_compact":"1","batch.max_concurrent": "1"}}'
```

alex: I'm pushing a quick patch to autoscaler to avoid immediate noisy scaleups for this flow (reduce burst to 0 for paged models). will monitor.

20m later — morgan: drained gcpu-034 and replaced with node gcpu-047. restarted runtime pods on 3 affected nodes. applied kv_compact and lowered batch. Observability: OOMs dropped to 0, paged_evictions spiked during compaction then trended down. latency back to normal for most customers.

lena: CS updated acme-inc: we applied mitigations and are monitoring, will follow up with postmortem. they acknowledged.

isha: good. next steps for postmortem: collect nvprof logs, heap snapshots, and allocation maps from the three replaced nodes. assign to sanjay and alex. Also add a canary in staging to run long-context workload to reproduce slow creep.

sanjay: taking postmortem ops — I'll bootstrap logs and upload to inc ticket. setting follow-up tasks: (1) root cause analysis of pager compaction not triggering earlier, (2) consider more aggressive periodic compaction or background defrag, (3) add alert for fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 over 30m.

alex: confirm we've turned off noisy autoscaler bursts and added model fallback policy for paged variants. I'll also prepare a quick rollback to q8 quantized variant if this appears again.

morgan: current status: OOMs stopped, latency good, customer impact contained. Handing off to night oncall. 

isha: handing to night oncall — sanjay. please watch fragmentation metrics and NV memory usage for 6h. escalate if fragmentation_ratio doesn't drop below 0.4.

sanjay: ack. will follow up in inc ticket with logs and remediation plan.

incident-bot: Incident inc-2026-04-12-836 status -> mitigated (monitoring). Followup: postmortem assigned.

alex: :thumbsup: summary will go into the incident ticket.
